einzeiler: Trisha reviews standout Canadian books ranging from non-fiction to romance and horror.
kurzfassung: Host Trisha celebrates Canadian authors and settings by discussing three diverse books on a weekly podcast. She highlights a true story about the aftermath of 9-11 in Gander, a contemporary romance set in Toronto, and a supernatural horror novel. The episode also features an audiobook excerpt from a sponsored fantasy title.
stichpunkte: Discussion of Canadian authors and stories set in Canada
Review of the non-fiction book The Day the World Came to Town by Jim DeFede about Gander, Newfoundland
Exploration of Much Ado About Nada by Uzma Jalaluddin as a retelling of Jane Austen's Persuasion
Analysis of the intersection between contemporary fiction and romance genres
Initial impressions of the horror novel Bad Cree by Jessica Johns
Audiobook excerpt from A Duel with the Vampire Lord by Elise Kova

clips.hook: A tiny town welcomes thousands of stranded passengers.
clips.text: Dozens of aircraft landed at a remote airfield in Newfoundland, carrying thousands of travelers into a community with a tiny population.

clips.hook: Avoiding a wedding by dodging the groom's brother.
clips.text: The protagonist attends a large cultural conference in Toronto alongside her best friend while intentionally staying away from a specific relative of the groom.

clips.hook: Reading scary stories only when daylight is on your side.
clips.text: The speaker explains that reading spooky fiction requires long summer days with plenty of sunshine to avoid getting too terrified.

clips.hook: Refusing to perish without dragging down the enemy.
clips.text: A weary combatant grips a heavy blade and vows to strike down her adversary before meeting her own end.

clips.hook: Carrying on a fallen sibling's mission to the very end.
clips.text: Determined to finish what her brother started, the heroine resolves to eliminate the vampire leader on behalf of her entire village.

beschreibung:
This week, Trisha recommends books about how great Canada is. From non-fiction to contemporary romantic fiction to horror, Canadian stories and Canadian writers are the best.

This content contains affiliate links. When you buy through these links, we may earn an affiliate commission.

Books Discussed

When the World Came to Town: 9/11 in Gander, Newfoundland by Jim DeFede

Much Ado About Nada by Uzma Jalaluddin

Bad Cree by Jessica Johns
